lessons.title: Fraction Division: Reciprocal Repair
lessons.concept: To divide by a nonzero fraction, multiply by its reciprocal.
guided: A mechanic has 3/4 liter of coolant; each bottle holds 1/4 liter. How many bottles?
guided_answers: 3 bottles. Divide 3/4 by 1/4: three quarter-liter portions fit.

lessons.title: Ratios: Find the Unit Rate
lessons.concept: A unit rate compares an amount with one unit. Divide first, then scale to the amount you need.

examples.problem: Three identical oil filters cost $27. What do five cost?
steps: Divide $27 by 3 filters to find $9 per filter.
Multiply 5 filters by $9 per filter to get $45.
Check: the cost per filter stays $9 when the quantity changes.

guided: Four identical belts cost $32. At the same rate, what do seven belts cost? Show the unit rate.
A student says six filters cost $30 because 27 + 3 = 30. Use the example to explain and correct the error.
guided_answers: $56. The unit rate is $32 / 4 = $8 per belt; 7 x $8 = $56.
$54. Six filters are twice as many as three, so double $27. Adding $3 does not keep the $9-per-filter rate.

lessons.title: Inequalities: Weight Limits
lessons.concept: At most includes the boundary; greater than does not include it.

examples.problem: A lift supports at most 2,000 pounds.
steps: Let w represent vehicle weight in pounds.
On a number line, use a filled circle at 2,000 and shade left.

guided: A workshop tool requires more than 12 volts. Write an inequality for v.
Decide whether 2,000 pounds is allowed by w <= 2000 and explain.
guided_answers: v > 12. Exactly 12 volts does not satisfy more than 12.
Yes. The <= symbol includes equality, so 2,000 pounds is allowed.

lessons.title: Coordinates: Move and Reflect
lessons.concept: In (x, y), x measures horizontal position and y measures vertical position. Reflection across the x-axis keeps x and reverses the sign of y.

examples.problem: A cart is at (-3, 2). Move it 5 units right, then reflect across the x-axis.
steps: Moving right increases x: -3 + 5 = 2. The cart is now at (2, 2).
Reflecting across the x-axis changes y from 2 to -2: (2, -2).
The reflected point is 2 units below the x-axis; x is unchanged.

guided: Start at (-4, 3) and move 6 units right. Give the new coordinates and explain which coordinate changes.
Reflect (-2, -5) across the x-axis. A student gets (2, -5). Explain and correct the error.
guided_answers: (2, 3). Moving right adds 6 to x: -4 + 6 = 2. The y-coordinate stays 3.
(-2, 5). Reflection across the x-axis changes the sign of y, not x. The student reflected across the y-axis.

lessons.title: Geometry: Surface Area or Volume?
lessons.concept: Surface area measures the outside faces in square units. Volume measures the space inside in cubic units.

examples.problem: A closed rectangular box is 4 in long, 3 in wide, and 2 in high. Find surface area and volume.
steps: Opposite faces come in pairs: two 4 x 3 faces, two 4 x 2 faces, and two 3 x 2 faces.
Add face areas: 2 x 12 + 2 x 8 + 2 x 6 = 52 square inches.
Multiply the three dimensions for volume: 4 x 3 x 2 = 24 cubic inches.

guided: A closed rectangular box measures 5 cm by 2 cm by 3 cm. Find its surface area; show the three pairs of faces.
A student adds 5 + 2 + 3 and reports a volume of 10 cubic centimeters. Explain the error and find the volume.
guided_answers: 62 square centimeters. The three face pairs have areas 2 x (5 x 2), 2 x (5 x 3), and 2 x (2 x 3); add 20 + 30 + 12.
30 cubic centimeters. Volume counts unit cubes and requires multiplication: 5 x 2 x 3 = 30. Adding lengths does not measure volume.

lessons.title: Statistics: Read the Repair Times
lessons.concept: The median is the middle sorted value; the mean is the sum divided by the count.
guided: Explain why a very long repair may make the mean larger than the median.
guided_answers: 15 minutes. Subtract the minimum from the maximum: 25 - 10 = 15.
An unusually long repair adds to the total used for the mean. The median depends on the middle position, so it may change less.
